 At Jabalpur

sentences.text:
This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.231/2023 dated 12.07.2023 registered at Police Station- Sanjeevani Nagar, District- Jabalpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467,
468, 471, 120-B/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 11.07.2023.
The applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He submits that no offence has been committed by the applicant and he bears no criminal record.
He submits that th e applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Trial will take considerable time to conclude.
Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
Learned counsel for the objector submits that he has no objection if the applicant is released on bail.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
In the present case, bail has been sought on behalf of the applicant on the ground that he has been wrongly implicated in the case and he has no criminal past.

According to the prosecution case, the applicant helped the co-accused Pankaj Thakur for preparing documents for housing loan and on the basis of those documents, co-accused persons hatched a conspiracy to get a fake sale- deed of the house of Anil Kewat executed and registered.
It may be mentioned here that Anil Kewat is being represented before this Court through his counsel, who has submitted no objection to the bail application of the present applicant.

Having considered these facts and also the act of applicant in commission of alleged crime, this Court finds it proper to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Prachi Arpit Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104099594/
